messages.subject: Formulating a specific mixture model
parts:
Hi folks,

I'm trying to figure out how to code a specific kind of mixture model. To get to the model, let me first describe a couple data-collection scenarios of increasing complexity:

[1] I show you a colored square briefly, then ask you to indicate its color by clicking a spot on a circular RGB color wheel. If we do this many times, each time measuring the radians of error in your response, we'd build up a distribution of responses that should be centered on zero error with some spread on either side, in which case the concentration parameter of a Von Mises distribution would be useful to quantify the fidelity of memory.

[2] Now, instead of a single square, I show you multiple squares, each of a different color. After a brief period, all the squares turn grey, and arrow appears pointing to one, and you're asked to indicate the color (on the color wheel as in [1]) of the pointed-to square. If you have perfect memory for the location-and-color combinations, then your responses should be distributed as in [1]. However, possibly your location-and-color combination memory is imperfect and on some proportion of trials you report the color from one of the other locations, but with the same fidelity with respect to that location's color as when reporting the color from the pointed-to location. 

I know that data from many repetitions of scenario [2] should form a mixture of a Von Mises and ... something, but I'm not sure how to formulate the second mixture component. Any suggestions? 

To make things more concrete, if there were 4 locations on every presentation trial, I imagine that I should be supplying the following as data

data {
int<lower=0> trial_count ;
real<lower=0,upper=2*pi()> error[trial_count] ;
        vector<lower=0,upper=2*pi()>[trial_count] wrongLocs[3] ;
}

where "error" contains the trial-by-trial radians of error (centered on pi; pi==0 radians of error) relative to the pointed-to-location, and "wrongLocs" conatains the trial-by-trial locations on the color wheel of the other 3 colors, again relative to the pointed-to-location. Fixing the fidelity (Von Mises concentration) parameter at 10 for simplicity, we might then have

parameters {
    real<lower=0,upper=1> mix_proportion ;
}
model {
    real ps[2] ;
    for( i in 1:trial_count ){
       ps[1] <- log(mix_proportion) + von_mises_log(error[i],pi,10)
       ps[2] <- log1m(mix_proportion) +???
       increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps))
    }  
}

So I'm trying to figure out what should replace the "???". Would it make sense for it to simply be:

ps[2] <- log1m(mix_proportion) + ( von_mises_log(error[i], wrongLocs[i][1],10) + von_mises_log(error[i], wrongLocs[i][2],10) + von_mises_log(error[i], wrongLocs[i][3],10) )

? 


Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.subject: Re: Formulating a specific mixture model
parts:
Sorry for answering my own question again; I clearly need to learn to take a little more time to try to solve things myself!

Anyway, I now realize (thanks to reading http://www.paulbays.com/pdf/BayCatHus09.pdf), that the proper way to implement this mixture would be:

model {
    real lps_to_sum_exp[3] ;

real ps[2]; 
    for( i in 1:trial_count ){

for( j in 1:3){
            lps_to_sum_exp[j] <- (1/3) + von_mises_log(error[i],wrongLocs[i][j],10)

}
        ps[1] <- log(mix_proportion) + von_mises_log(error[i],pi,10)

ps[2] <- log1m(mix_proportion) + log_sum_exp(lps_to_sum_exp)
        increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps))
    }  
}

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

> On Feb 28, 2015, at 6:10 AM, Mike Lawrence <mike....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Sorry for answering my own question again; I clearly need to learn to take a little more time to try to solve things myself!
>
> Anyway, I now realize (thanks to reading http://www.paulbays.com/pdf/BayCatHus09.pdf), that the proper way to implement this mixture would be:
>
> model {
> real lps_to_sum_exp[3] ;
> real ps[2];
> for( i in 1:trial_count ){
> for( j in 1:3){

> lps_to_sum_exp[j] <- von_mises_log(error[i],wrongLocs[i][j],10)
> }

As of Stan 2.6, you can replace this:

> ps[1] <- log(mix_proportion) + von_mises_log(error[i],pi,10)
> ps[2] <- log1m(mix_proportion) + log_sum_exp(lps_to_sum_exp)
> increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps))

with

increment_log_prob(log_mix(mix_proportion,
von_mises_log(error[i],pi,10),
log_sum_exp(lps_to_sum_exp) ));


And just to be clear, this produces a mixture of top-level models like
your example, not a mixture at the element level, as is more traditional
in mixture modeling. I'd think from your description you'd want to mix
at the element level, allowing varying memory among the subjects.

- Bob
